claim: Open ground under a lower sky between tall buildings cuts their sides at its sky line, and above it each building is a front with nothing behind it. The court takes the street's sky and its sides wear the neighbours' facade round the corner; a low front's height belongs to a thin lip (about 128 deep) before it.
evidence: The owner, 2026-11-25: the forecourt 'makes buildings next to it to look like paper thin because of the sky'.
Exemplar of a roofed, columned portico giving the mass depth: E1M7 s12.
use: Run the thin-front check after any change of sky height.
